summary:
Ondo is a state in south-western Nigeria and stands under the national framework: the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 applies here as it does across the country, and the sources record no Ondo statute, protective measure or enforcement divergence of the state's own. The Wikipedia overview of LGBT rights in Nigeria does not name Ondo at all, and no state-level anti-discrimination protection or recognition of gender identity is recorded for it.

The Shari'a penalty layer does not reach Ondo. The twelve states operating Shari'a-based criminal codes, where male sodomy can carry the death penalty, lie in the north of the country; Ondo, in the south, sits under the secular framework, for which the same source records a maximum penalty of a life sentence in the southern portion of the country.

The offence that applies in Ondo is the gross-indecency felony. Section 217 of the Criminal Code makes any male who commits or procures an act of gross indecency with another male, in public or private, guilty of a felony liable to three years' imprisonment. The UK Home Office country policy and information note cites Victor Oluwasina Ayeni, a senior lecturer in law at Adekunle Ajasin University in Ondo state, who observed in a January 2017 book chapter that the Code does not define what constitutes an act of gross indecency, which leaves the reach of the offence to police and prosecutorial discretion.

No enforcement specific to Ondo is documented. The sources contain no arrest, raid, prosecution, venue closure or police-command statement in the state; the mass arrests and venue closures in the national record are located in other states.
tangentialFactors:
Ondo's legal position is entirely derivative. The state has enacted nothing of its own on sexual orientation or gender identity, and the sources attribute no state-level protective or restrictive statute to it, so exposure in Ondo is set by national law and by the discretion of the state police command rather than by any Ondo instrument.

The UK Home Office note records countrywide patterns of arrest, detention and mob violence against LGBT+ people and identifies no divergence specific to Ondo. A visitor should therefore expect the national pattern rather than a distinct local one.
localsOnly:
No Ondo statute provides anti-discrimination protection or recognition of a partner relationship, and no state-level instrument on either is recorded. Any legal step on documents or status has to be taken under national law.

Because the Criminal Code leaves gross indecency undefined, the conduct that attracts a charge in Ondo is determined in practice by the state police and prosecutors rather than by the text of the statute.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Ondo-specific enforcement data were located: the sources contain no arrest, prosecution or conviction figures for the state, no statement from the Ondo state police command, and no Ondo court ruling. Whether Ondo applies the gross-indecency offence at a different rate from other southern states is unresolved on these sources.

The Wikipedia overview does not name Ondo, and the UK Home Office note's Ondo-linked material is a January 2017 book chapter. The current enforcement posture of the state is not documented in the sources reviewed.
